The statutory provisions generally deal with the rights and duties of particular parties rather than with the privileges that accrue because of the relative positions of adjoining pieces of land.
. Water Classification
Water generally moves from the upper to lower land in one of the following ways:
a. channel waters
b. surface waters
c. flood waters
d. percolating waters
Rights of drainage are, to a degree, contingent on the manner in which water moves from one property to another. In Illinois there appears to be no distinction in application of the rule of natural drainage between channel, surface and flood waters. Percolating water, on the other hand, passes through the ground beneath the earth's surface without a definite channel. This type of water is part of the land itself and belongs to the owner of the land. The rules of natural drainage are applicable to intermittent as well as continuous flowing water in channels.
RESTORATION OF ORIGINAL DRAINAGE
It is the purpose of the Division to accommodate affected landowners in drainage matters to the extent of the State's obligation and to provide protection against excessive construction costs.
When planning an improvement to a new or existing highway, the Division will not destroy or reduce individual rights concerning the handling of drainage waters. When drainage systems are intercepted by improvements sponsored by the State, the drainage system shall be restored to the approximate standard that existed prior to the construction of the highway. It is not the obligation of the Division to improve drainage or protect adjacent properties from potential flooding.
